'''Jayson Christopher Tatum Sr.''' ({{IPAc-en |ˈ|t|eɪ|t|ə|m}} {{respell|TAY|təm}}; born March 3, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] in high school in [[Missouri]] and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. Tatum was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the third overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] and was voted to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] in the [[2017–18 NBA season|2018 season]]. Tatum won the inaugural [[NBA conference finals MVP awards|NBA Eastern Conference finals MVP]] in [[2022 NBA playoffs|2022]], and won his first title in the [[2024 NBA Finals]].

Nicknamed "'''the Anomaly'''",<ref>{{cite web|last=Flores|first=Geca|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/jayson-tatums-reaction-strange-nickname-013416640.html|title=Jayson Tatum's Reaction to Strange Nickname Leaves Travis Kelce, Jason Kelce in Stitches|work=[[Athlon Sports]]|via=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=March 26, 2025|accessdate=June 20, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Roche|first=Conor|url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2025/03/09/jayson-tatum-nickname-the-anomaly-player-a-big-deuce/|title=Jayson Tatum settles nickname debate following emergence of 'The Anomaly'|website=[[Boston.com]]|date=March 9, 2025|accessdate=June 20, 2025}}</ref> Tatum is a six-time [[NBA All-Star]] and five-time [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA selection]] (including four first-team selections). He and [[Jaylen Brown]] made up the Celtics' "[[Jays (Boston Celtics)|Jays]]" duo from Tatum’s rookie season until 2026. In 2024, Tatum led the team to a league-best 64 wins and a championship in the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. Tatum also won a gold medal with the [[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2020]] and [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2024 U.S. Olympic team]]s.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/jayson-tatum_1954684 |title=TATUM Jayson |work=[[Paris 2024 Olympics]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007153124/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/jayson-tatum_1954684 |archive-date=October 7, 2024}}</ref> He holds the records for most points scored in an [[NBA All-Star Game]] (55), most points scored in a [[Game seven|Game 7]] of any [[NBA playoffs]] series (51), and most points scored in the [[NBA playoffs]] at his age.

==High school career==
Tatum attended [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (Missouri)|Chaminade College Preparatory School]] in [[Creve Coeur, Missouri]]. He was inspired by [[Bradley Beal]], a senior at Chaminade, while Tatum was in his first year there as a seventh grader. Tatum struggled with the school's college preparatory curriculum, and his classmates were substantially more privileged than he was. Tatum played alongside [[Tyler Cook]] and was in gym class with classmate [[Matthew Tkachuk]]. Tatum wanted to play under his father, the head basketball coach at nearby [[Christian Brothers College High School]], but his mother preferred Chaminade so Tatum would still work hard on academics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 15, 2015 |title=It's not hype if you can do it, and Chaminade's Jayson Tatum can |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/other/its-not-hype-if-you-can-do-it-and-chaminades-jayson-tatum-can |access-date=2024-06-20 |website=FOX Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="godfather">{{Cite web |last=Hochman |first=Benjamin |date=2015-11-19 |title=Hochman: Like godfather, like godson — Jayson Tatum is on track for NBA |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/hochman-like-godfather-like-godson-jayson-tatum-is-on-track-for-nba/article_9599b815-ebc5-5a6a-8743-1cd389e3b0a7.html |access-date=2024-06-20 |website=STLtoday.com |language=en}}</ref>

As a freshman, Tatum averaged 13.3 points and 6.4 rebounds per game and was named 2013 Metro Catholic Conference (MCC) Co-Player of the Year, leading the Red Devils to both MCC and Missouri District 2 crowns.

As a sophomore in 2014, Tatum averaged 26.0 points and 11.0 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Niesen |first=Joan |date=2015-04-21 |title=Jayson Tatum, 2016's top recruit, faces a tough choice |url=https://www.si.com/college/2015/04/21/recruiting-jayson-tatum-class-2016-missouri |access-date=2024-06-20 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref>

As a junior, Tatum averaged 25.9 points, 11.7 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game, while earning Second-team Naismith Trophy All-American honors. In the summer of 2015, he joined the St. Louis Eagles [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team on the highly competitive [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) Circuit. On July 11, the Eagles narrowly defeated future [[Duke Blue Devils|Duke]] teammate [[Harry Giles (basketball)|Harry Giles]] and Team CP3 74–73 in the Nike Peach Jam Semi-Finals with a game-winning buzzer-beater to advance to the championship game, where Tatum finished the game with 28 points and five rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Cam |date=July 12, 2015 |title=Nike EYBL Peach Jam: Before picking Duke, Jayson Tatum sparked the end of Team CP3's run |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/nike-eybl-peach-jam-before-picking-duke-jayson-tatum-sparked-the-end-of-team-cp3s-run |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150714053332/http://usatodayhss.com/2015/nike-eybl-peach-jam-before-picking-duke-jayson-tatum-sparked-the-end-of-team-cp3s-run |archive-date=July 14, 2015 |access-date=July 11, 2015 |website=USA Today High School Sports}}</ref> The next day, he had 24 points, seven rebounds, and four blocks in a 104–77 loss to the Georgia Stars and future Duke [[Eligibility for the NBA draft|one-and-done]] [[Wendell Carter Jr.]] in the 2015 Nike Peach Jam championship game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/nike-eybl-peach-jam-wendell-carters-georgia-stars-rout-jayson-tatums-st-louis-eagles-to-claim-tourney-eybl-title |title=Nike EYBL Peach Jam: Wendell Carter's Georgia Stars rout Jayson Tatum's St. Louis Eagles to claim tourney EYBL title |last=Smith |first=Cam |date=July 12, 2015 |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=January 5, 2016 |archive-date=January 6, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160106224725/http://usatodayhss.com/2015/nike-eybl-peach-jam-wendell-carters-georgia-stars-rout-jayson-tatums-st-louis-eagles-to-claim-tourney-eybl-title |url-status=live}}</ref> During the Circuit, Tatum led the EYBL in scoring with 26.5 points to go along with 9.5 rebounds per game.

Before his senior year, Tatum made a verbal commitment to [[Duke University]] over [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], and [[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis University]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/13244364/jayson-tatum-no-2-recruit-espn-class-2016-commits-duke-blue-devils |title=Jayson Tatum commits to Duke |last=Biancardi |first=Paul |date=July 12, 2015 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 12, 2015 |archive-date=February 22, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180222230154/http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/13244364/jayson-tatum-no-2-recruit-espn-class-2016-commits-duke-blue-devils |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/mens-basketball/article27080620.html |title=Five-star forward Jayson Tatum commits to Duke |last=Keeley |first=Laura |date=July 12, 2015 |publisher=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |access-date=July 12, 2015 |archive-date=December 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181208180045/https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/mens-basketball/article27080620.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Boston Celtics]] general manager [[Danny Ainge]] traded the team's [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|No. 1 overall pick]] in the [[2017 NBA draft]] to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for the third overall pick, which the Celtics used to select Jayson Tatum. Tatum was the Celtics' second consecutive No. 3 pick for a small forward, following [[Jaylen Brown]] in 2016, whom Tatum formed a [[Jays (Boston Celtics)|duo]] with.<ref>{{cite web |first=Chris |last=Forsberg |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19711028/2017-nba-draft-boston-celtics-take-jayson-tatum-no-3-overall-pick |title=Duke's Jayson Tatum selected No. 3 overall by Celtics |work=ESPN.com |date=June 22, 2017 |access-date=April 28, 2018 |archive-date=November 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111222714/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19711028/2017-nba-draft-boston-celtics-take-jayson-tatum-no-3-overall-pick |url-status=live}}</ref> During the [[2017 NBA Summer League]] event in Utah, Tatum averaged 18.7 points, 9.7 rebounds, 2.3 steals, and 2.0 assists in nearly 33 minutes of action. Later, in Las Vegas, Tatum produced similar results, averaging 17.7 points, 8.0 rebounds, 1.0 assists, and 0.8 blocks in nearly 32 minutes of action in three games. ==== 2024–25 season: Record-breaking extension and season ending Achilles rupture====
On July 1, 2024, Tatum signed a five-year contract extension worth up to $314 million, surpassing his superstar teammate Jaylen Brown's $304 million extension as the richest deal in NBA history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2024 |title=Sources: Celtics' Jayson Tatum agrees to 5-year, $314M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40476501/sources-celtics-jayson-tatum-agrees-5-year-314m-extension |access-date=July 1, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On November 16, 2024, Tatum put up 24 points, 11 rebounds, and nine assists, alongside a buzzer-beating, game-winning three-pointer in a 126–123 overtime win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtics' Jayson Tatum breaks the internet with wild OT game-winner vs. Raptors |url=https://clutchpoints.com/celtics-news-jayson-tatum-breaks-internet-wild-ot-game-winner-raptors |website=ClutchPoints |last=Smith |first=Christopher |date=November 16, 2024 |access-date=November 16, 2024}}</ref> On December 21, Tatum scored a season-high 43 points along with 15 rebounds and 10 assists in a 123–98 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]]. He became just the fifth player in NBA history to record 40+ points, 15+ rebounds, 10+ assists and 5+ 3s in a game, joining [[James Harden]] (2x), [[DeMarcus Cousins]], [[Russell Westbrook]] and [[Vince Carter]]. Tatum is also the first player in Celtics history to record 40+ points, 15+ boards and 10+ dimes in a game. He also joined [[Larry Bird]] as the only Celtics with 40-point triple-doubles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 22, 2024 |title=Starting 5, Dec. 22: Jayson Tatum & Victor Wembanyama shine bright |url=https://www.nba.com/news/starting-5-dec-22-jayson-tatum-victor-wembanyama-shine-bright |access-date=December 22, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2024/12/21/sports/celtics-bulls-game-score-jayson-tatum/|title=Jayson Tatum posts historic triple-double as Celtics quickly avenge loss to Bulls with blowout win in Chicago|last=Washburn|first=Gary|publisher=[[The Boston Globe]].|date=December 21, 2024|accessdate=December 22, 2024}}</ref>

On January 25, 2025, Tatum was named an [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] starter for the [[2025 NBA All-Star Game]], marking his sixth consecutive selection and his third selection in a row as a starter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Giannis Antetokounmpo, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander highlight All-Star starters |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-all-star-game-starters |access-date=January 25, 2025 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> On February 20, Tatum put up his fourth career triple-double with 15 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 124–104 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/boston-celtics/celtics-news-joe-mazzulla-jayson-tatum-opinion-triple-double-76ers |title=Joe Mazzulla's honest Jayson Tatum opinion after triple-double vs. 76ers |website=ClutchPoints |last=Yasis |first=Nathan |date=February 21, 2025 |access-date=February 21, 2025}}</ref> On February 28, Tatum recorded season-highs with 46 points and 16 rebounds along with nine assists and three blocks in a 123–116 loss against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. He had 30 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in the opening 24 minutes, the first player ever to reach those totals in a half during the play-by-play era (1997–98).<ref>{{cite web |date=March 1, 2025 |title=Mitchell scores 41, Cavaliers overcome 22-point deficit to beat the Celtics 123-116 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705418 |access-date=March 1, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On April 29, in Game 5 of the first round of the playoffs, Tatum scored 35 points on 10-for-16 shooting, 4-for-5 from 3-point range and a perfect 11-for-11 from the free-throw line, to go along with eight rebounds and 10 assists in a 120–89 close-out win over the [[Orlando Magic]]. Tatum became the first player in NBA history to make 10-plus free throws without a miss in three consecutive playoff games. He went 37 for 37 at the free throw line over a three-game span and missed just four free throws in the entire five-game series (37-for-41). He also had three straight playoff games with 35-plus points to become only the second Celtics' player to accomplish that feat, joining Larry Bird.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 30, 2025 |title=Tatum makes more NBA playoff history with dominant Game 5 vs. Magic |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/tatum-makes-more-nba-playoff-235857979.html?guccounter=1 |access-date=April 30, 2025 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> On May 12, in Game 4 of the second round of the playoffs, Tatum scored 42 points, along with eight rebounds, four assists, four steals, and two blocks, in a 121–113 loss to the [[New York Knicks]]. He also tied Larry Bird and [[John Havlicek]] for the most 40-point playoff games in Celtics franchise history with five.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/boston-celtics/celtics-news-jayson-tatum-celtics-history-before-leaving-game-4|title=Jayson Tatum makes Celtics history before leaving Game 4|website=ClutchPoints|last=Yasis|first=Nathan|date=May 12, 2025|access-date=May 12, 2025}}</ref> However, in the final minutes of the fourth quarter, Tatum suffered a [[Achilles tendon rupture|ruptured Achilles tendon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2025/05/13/sport/knicks-win-game-five-jayson-tatum-injury-spt|title=Knicks come up huge at home to take 3-1 lead over Celtics as Boston loses star to apparent leg injury|website=CNN|last=Sterling|first=Wayne|date=May 12, 2025|access-date=May 12, 2025}}</ref> He had surgery to repair it the next day, and was sidelined for the rest of the playoffs,<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.nba.com/news/celtics-jayson-tatum-surgery-ruptured-right-achilles|title= Celtics' Jayson Tatum undergoes surgery to repair ruptured Achilles tendon|website=NBA.com|last=Hightower|first=Kyle|date=May 14, 2025|access-date=May 14, 2025}}</ref> which ended in a 119–81 loss in Game 6.<ref>{{Cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date=May 16, 2025 |title=Knicks beat Celtics 119-81 in Game 6 and advance to face Pacers in Eastern Conference finals |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401769751 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=March 10, 2026}}</ref>

==== 2025–26 season: Recovery from injury ====
Ten months after rupturing his Achilles, Tatum returned and made his [[2025–26 Boston Celtics season|2025–26 season]] debut on March 6, 2026, against the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]], in which he recorded 15 points along with 12 rebounds and seven assists in a 120–100 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jayson Tatum scores 15 points in return from Achilles surgery, Celtics beat Mavericks 120-100 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401810763 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> On April 1, Tatum notched his fifth career triple-double with 25 points, 18 rebounds, and 11 assists in a 147–129 win over the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Recap: Jayson Tatum's return from Achilles surgery has impressed this NBA legend |url=https://www.nba.com/news/jayson-tatum-return-from-injury |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Recap: Victor Wembanyama drops 41, leads Spurs to 26th win in 28 games |url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-jayson-tatums-celtics-face-bam-adebayos-heat-on-espn |access-date=2026-04-02 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> 

In the playoffs, Tatum averaged 23.3 points, 10.7 rebounds, and a playoff career-high 6.8 assists per game. The Celtics were eliminated in the [[2026 NBA playoffs#(2) Boston Celtics vs. (7) Philadelphia 76ers |Eastern Conference First Round]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] after a hard-fought seven-game series. Tatum missed Game 7 due to left knee stiffness, and the Celtics fell 109–100 to the 76ers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jayson Tatum (knee) out against 76ers in Game 7 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/jayson-tatum-knee-out-against-76ers-in-game-7 |website=NBA.com |access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Joel Embiid leads 76ers to 109-100 Game 7 win over Celtics to complete comeback from 3-1 deficit |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401869412 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>
